p7_b0.ocr: In the study by Shah et al. [106] conducted in 1991 involving 7 PD patients, the antioxidant used was 100 mg ascorbic acid/day over a study period of 4 weeks, resulting in ↑ 45% in serum ascorbic acid levels. Ando et al. [100] in 1999 studied 16 CAPD patients with 1.8 gr EPA/day for 12 weeks, which led to ↓ serum ox-LDL levels. Islam et al. [101] in 2000 examined 17 PD patients, administering 800 IU AT/day for 12 weeks, resulting in ↓ susceptibility of LDL oxidation, ↑ 217% serum lipid- standardized AT, and ↑ 135% serum LDL AT levels.

p7_b1.ocr: O' Byrne et al. [104] in 2001 also studied 17 PD patients with 800 IU AT/day for 12 weeks, achieving ↑ serum LDL AT levels with no effect on autoantibodies to ox-LDL. Diepeveen et al. [102] in 2005 researched 21 PD patients receiving 40 mg atorvastatin/day over 12 weeks, resulting in ↓ serum ox-LDL levels, improved lipid profile, and no effect on in vitro LDL oxidizability. Another study in 2005 with 800 IU AT/day over 12 weeks noted no effect on serum ox-LDL levels, no effect on lipid profile, and ↓ in vitro LDL oxidizability. Domenici et al.
